_readme: PVill demo organization profiles. Hardcode these. Facts come from each organization's official page, checked Oct 17, 2026.
demoAccountEmail is FAKE. It uses example.org, a domain reserved for examples, so it can never belong to a real organization.
publicPhone, publicEmail, and publicAddress are real public contact details from the official pages. Use them on cards and details screens. Use demoAccountEmail only for the demo account or sign-in.
null means not listed on the official page. Show 'Not listed'. Do not guess.
centerZip and radiusMiles are DEMO APPROXIMATIONS used only for the 15-mile ranking. The organizations did not publish a radius.
Show the badge 'Public listing' on these profiles, not 'Verified'. These organizations have not verified themselves with PVill.
Do not attach sample items to these real organizations. Sample items belong to the made-up organizations (KAN-26).

organizations.name: Nurses for Newborns Tennessee
organizations.about: Nurses visit expecting parents and families with babies. They give care, teaching, and help finding other support.
organizations.whoWeServe: Families who are pregnant, and families with babies up to 12 months who meet the program's rules.
organizations.areaServed: Cheatham, Davidson, Dickson, Maury, Montgomery, Robertson, Rutherford, Sumner, Williamson, and Wilson counties
organizations.referralOrAppointment: Referral needed from a health care or social service provider. No self-referral.
organizations.nextStep: Ask your health care provider, social worker, or case manager to send a referral. Call 615-313-9989 with questions.

organizations.name: Nashville Diaper Connection
organizations.about: Gets diapers to families through local partner groups and programs.
organizations.whoWeServe: Families who need diapers. Access depends on the partner group and program.
organizations.referralOrAppointment: Diapers come through partner groups. Check the partner's rules.
organizations.nextStep: Open Get Diapers on the website, find a partner near you, and confirm hours and what to bring.
organizations.limits: Families do not get diapers from the office directly.

organizations.name: Foster Families Assistance Network (FFAN)
organizations.about: Gives foster, kinship, and adoptive families clothing, personal care items, undergarments, toys, and other basics at no cost.
organizations.referralOrAppointment: Not listed. Contact first to confirm what is in stock.
organizations.publicAddress: 13 Industrial Park Dr, Suite 100, Hendersonville, TN
organizations.publicContactNote: Contact through its Facebook page: https://www.facebook.com/FFAN16
organizations.nextStep: Message FFAN on Facebook, then visit the resource center to pick what you need.
organizations.limits: For foster, kinship, and adoptive placements. Items in stock change.

organizations.name: TennCare Diaper Benefit
organizations.about: Up to 100 diapers a month at no cost for children under 2. Get them at a participating pharmacy.
organizations.whoWeServe: Children under 2 who are enrolled in TennCare or CoverKids.
organizations.referralOrAppointment: No prescription needed. Bring the child's pharmacy ID card.
organizations.nextStep: Use the website's pharmacy map to find a participating pharmacy. Bring the child's pharmacy ID card. Ask what diaper types are in stock.
organizations.limits: Needs TennCare or CoverKids enrollment. Brands and sizes vary by pharmacy. Diapers only.

organizations.name: Nashville Foster Love Closet and Resource Center
organizations.about: Gives materials, resources, and support to children and families involved with foster care.
organizations.whoWeServe: Children and families involved with foster care.
organizations.referralOrAppointment: Not listed. Contact first to confirm what is available.
organizations.nextStep: Email the closet, say what your family needs, and ask how to pick it up.
organizations.limits: For families involved with foster care. Supplies change.

organizations.name: Davidson County WIC
organizations.about: Healthy food, nutrition help, breastfeeding support, and referrals from pregnancy until a child's fifth birthday.
organizations.whoWeServe: Pregnant and new parents, babies, and children under 5, if they meet WIC rules.
organizations.publicAddress: Lentz Public Health Center, 2500 Charlotte Avenue, Nashville, TN 37209
organizations.publicContactNote: Other clinics: East Public Health Center 615-862-6626, South Nashville WIC Nutrition Center 615-880-3210, Woodbine Public Health Center 615-880-2299.
organizations.nextStep: Fill out the WIC Interest Form on the website, or call a clinic to set an appointment.
organizations.limits: Davidson County residents. Bring proof of identity, address, and income.

organizations.name: Davidson County WIC Breastfeeding Support
organizations.about: Help getting ready to breastfeed, solving common problems, going back to work or school, and getting a breast pump when it is right. Support is the same if you breastfeed, use formula, or both.
organizations.whoWeServe: Families getting WIC in Davidson County, before and after the baby is born.
organizations.publicAddress: Lentz Public Health Center, 2500 Charlotte Avenue, Nashville, TN 37209
organizations.nextStep: Contact a Davidson County WIC clinic and ask for breastfeeding support.
organizations.limits: A breast pump is not automatic. It is given when it is right for the family.

organizations.name: MySimilac Rewards
organizations.about: Savings offers and coupons on Similac formula. It is not free formula.
organizations.whoWeServe: Families who use or may use Similac. One sign-up for each home.
organizations.nextStep: Sign up on the website. Read the current offer and the privacy terms. Signing up includes marketing messages.
organizations.limits: Savings only. Offers and values change. One sign-up for each home.

organizations.name: Grace Place
organizations.about: Long-term housing with life skills classes, mentoring, community meals, and faith-based care for single mothers and their children.
organizations.referralOrAppointment: Application and orientation. Openings must be confirmed.
organizations.nextStep: Use I Need Help on the website, call 615-881-3976, or email to ask about the program and how to apply.
organizations.limits: This is a program, not an emergency shelter. It does not promise an opening.

organizations.name: Ella's House
organizations.about: Housing, community, and mental health and wellness help so student mothers can have their babies and finish their degrees.
organizations.whoWeServe: Pregnant and parenting students at colleges in the greater Nashville area.
organizations.nextStep: Call 615-656-0824 or email to ask about housing and student support.
organizations.limits: For students who are pregnant or parenting. Not general housing for all parents. Availability must be confirmed.

organizations.name: Sweet Cheeks Diaper Bank
organizations.about: Gets diapers and period products to families through local nonprofits and health care partners.
organizations.whoWeServe: Families in the Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky area who go to a partner group.
organizations.referralOrAppointment: Diapers come through partner groups. Call the partner to confirm hours and what to bring.
organizations.nextStep: Use the partner map on the website. Search by ZIP code, city, or partner name. Call the number listed.
organizations.limits: Not statewide Kentucky coverage. Show only when the person widens the distance.

organizations.name: Food Bank of North Alabama Diaper Bank
organizations.about: Gets diapers to trusted community partner groups that serve families in North Alabama.
organizations.whoWeServe: Families across North Alabama through partner groups.
organizations.referralOrAppointment: Families get diapers from partner groups, not from the food bank directly.
organizations.nextStep: Open the website and contact the food bank to find a partner group near you.
organizations.limits: Show only when the person widens the distance.
